name: Compile devtools nodes out behind a feature

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Compile devtools nodes out behind a feature

Mechanism: a `devtools` feature (default, and in test-support) gates recording the per-element DevKit node, its semantics and property setters, and copying them in reused and spliced stretches, through a `DEVTOOLS` const so the dead branches are not compiled. Text elements build their semantics lazily. Triggered by the user's request to compile it out behind a flag; a probe that stubbed the node recording gave -15% CPU on dashboard-clock. Allowed: Cargo.toml, window.rs, splice.rs, text.rs, docs. Forbidden: any other behaviour change.
measurementPlanMarkdown: bm.sh e05 over nine scenarios, 3 reps, benchmark builds with default-features=false (feature off). Pass: dashboard-clock CPU down at least 10% with fast mode on, no scenario worse than noise, devtools tests green with the feature on, clippy clean with it off.

measurements.metric: dashboard-clock on CPU / draw p50 / allocs per frame
heap peak, fast on (all nine scenarios)

reportMarkdown:
## Compile devtools nodes out behind a feature Finished

Passed: true. With the feature off nothing builds, copies or drops a DevKit node per element, and text elements stop allocating their semantics strings every frame. CPU falls 1-16% with fast mode on, allocations per frame 6-62%, heap peak 3-12%. With the feature on (the default) behaviour is unchanged: `devtools` (2), `semantic_locators` (13), `devtools_snapshot_tree` (1) and `fast::tests::splice` (8) pass; `cargo clippy -p gpux --no-default-features -D warnings` is clean. The off configuration is proven by the benchmark runs; test-support turns the feature on, so no unit test runs with it off.

Attempt Count: 1. Out-of-scope changes: none (a docs paragraph describes the feature).
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Committed success. Consumers keep today's behaviour through the default features; opting out is `default-features = false`.
